hello.note: Works any time of day, with anyone. Selam is a casual hi

good-night.note: Also a goodbye in the evening. Good evening is İyi akşamlar (ee-YEE ak-sham-LAR)

goodbye.note: Said by the one leaving. The one staying says Güle güle (gü-LEH gü-LEH), go smiling

thank-you.note: Shorter: teşekkürler, or sağ olun. The reply is rica ederim

no.note: Often said with a quick upward nod and a click of the tongue

excuse-me.note: Both sorry and excuse me. Pardon also works

its-beautiful.note: Güzel is beautiful and also good: çok güzel, very nice

dont-understand.note: One word: Turkish builds sentences by adding endings

speak-english.note: Mu and its forms (mı, mi, mü) turn a sentence into a yes/no question

hundred.note: Just yüz, with no one in front

thousand.note: Prices are in lira: yüz lira is 100 lira

hundred-thousand.note: Written 100.000: Turkey marks thousands with a dot

how-much.note: Point and say Bu ne kadar? (boo NEH kah-dar), how much is this?

would-like.note: Literally can I have ...?, the polite way to order. The audio uses bir çay (bir CHAY), a tea, as the example

i-want.note: Direct, and fine in shops. The thing comes first; the audio uses bunu (BOO-noo), this one

do-you-have.note: Literally is there ...? Su var mı? = do you have water?

discount.note: Haggling is expected in bazaars, not in shops with price tags

card.note: Literally does a credit card go through? Cards are taken almost everywhere

checkout-time.note: Saat kaçta? means at what time? for anything

breakfast.note: A Turkish breakfast is a feast worth getting up for

toilet.note: ... nerede? means where is ...? for anything. Signs say WC, Bay (men) and Bayan (women)

taxi.note: Yellow taxis run on a meter, the taksimetre

bus.note: City buses and long-distance coaches alike

bus-station.note: The long-distance bus station, usually outside the city center

which-train.note: The city comes first and takes -a or -e, meaning to: Ankara'ya. The audio uses Ankara

two-tickets.note: Iki is two; üç (3) or dört (4) for more. The audio uses Ankara'ya, to Ankara

trip-length.note: Literally to ..., how long does it take? The audio uses Ankara

delicious.note: To thank the cook, say Ellerinize sağlık, health to your hands

allergic.note: The food comes first: fıstık alerjim var, I'm allergic to peanuts

love-dish.note: Literally I fainted for this dish, the usual way to say you love it

beer.note: Efes is the usual beer. Not every restaurant serves alcohol

coffee.note: Turkish coffee is ordered by sweetness: sade (none), orta (medium) or şekerli (sweet)

tea.note: Drunk all day from small tulip-shaped glasses

hot.note: Hot, and hot weather. Spicy is acı (ah-JUH)

cold.note: Cold, for drinks and the weather

pharmacy.note: Look for the red E sign. A nöbetçi eczane is the pharmacy on night duty
